hints.title: Ternary Profile State
hints.text: Represent the occupants of the previous n cells as a ternary state (0 for empty, 1 for introvert, 2 for extrovert).

hints.title: Evaluate Cell and Neighbor Happiness Delta
hints.text: When placing an introvert or extrovert at (r, c), compute their base happiness and adjust for left and upper neighbors.

hints.title: Memoize by Cell and Counts
hints.text: Memoize states using tuple (cell_idx, introverts_left, extroverts_left, profile_tuple).

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from functools import lru_cache

class Solution:
    def getMaxGridHappiness(self, m: int, n: int, introvertsCount: int, extrovertsCount: int) -> int:
        if m < n:
            m, n = n, m
        total_cells = m * n

        @lru_cache(maxsize=None)
        def dp(pos: int, ic: int, ec: int, profile: tuple) -> int:
            if pos == total_cells or (ic == 0 and ec == 0):
                return 0
            r, c = divmod(pos, n)
            up = profile[0]
            left = profile[-1] if c > 0 else 0

            # 1. Leave cell empty
            ans = dp(pos + 1, ic, ec, profile[1:] + (0,))

            # 2. Place Introvert (1)
            if ic > 0:
                cost = 120
                if up == 1: cost -= 60
                elif up == 2: cost -= 10
                if left == 1: cost -= 60
                elif left == 2: cost -= 10
                ans = max(ans, cost + dp(pos + 1, ic - 1, ec, profile[1:] + (1,)))

            # 3. Place Extrovert (2)
            if ec > 0:
                cost = 40
                if up == 1: cost -= 10
                elif up == 2: cost += 40
                if left == 1: cost -= 10
                elif left == 2: cost += 40
                ans = max(ans, cost + dp(pos + 1, ic, ec - 1, profile[1:] + (2,)))

            return ans

        init_profile = tuple([0] * n)
        return dp(0, introvertsCount, extrovertsCount, init_profile)
```

variables: m and n are grid dimensions (m * n <= 25, n <= 5)
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing 3^(m * n) configurations evaluates up to 3^25 states, which is 8 * 10^11 combinations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Profile DP keeps a sliding window of the last n cells (3^5 = 243 states), making memoized search fast.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate recognizes profile/broken-profile DP over n <= 5 width with ternary state encoding.
